subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw make memory trust/provenance a native memory contract across default backends, or leave trust-scored memories to external MCP/plugin packages for now?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the solution defines security boundaries, public memory/plugin contracts, persisted schema, config policy, and retrieval behavior that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design native trust metadata
options.body: Keep #7707 open as the canonical thread for framework-assigned source trust, persisted memory metadata, retrieval-time policy, and migration/SDK changes.

options.title: Stage behind provenance MVP
options.body: Resolve durable provenance and source-attribution issues such as #42647 and #48519 first, then layer trust scoring, review gates, and expiration policy on top.

options.title: Defer to external plugins
options.body: Close or split this only if maintainers decide current MCP/plugin seams are sufficient and OpenClaw should not own default memory trust enforcement yet.

recommendation.title: Design native trust metadata
recommendation.body: Keep #7707 open as the canonical thread for framework-assigned source trust, persisted memory metadata, retrieval-time policy, and migration/SDK changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest routing signal for the memory host SDK and memory-core contract boundary and has prior review context on this issue.
